CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted name] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Maternal Age: 40 years
Gestational Age at Amniocentesis: 17 weeks by ultrasound
Indication for Testing: Advanced maternal age, screening for Down syndrome and other chromosomal abnormalities

PREVIOUS TESTING
Rapid PCR analysis for common aneuploidies performed on [redacted date]
Result: Negative for trisomies 13, 18, and 21

CURRENT TEST PERFORMED
G-banded Chromosome Analysis (Karyotype)

METHODOLOGY
Amniotic fluid cells were cultured using standard cytogenetic techniques. Metaphase chromosomes were harvested and G-banded using trypsin-Giemsa staining. A minimum of 20 metaphase cells were analyzed at the 400-550 band level of resolution. Five cells were fully karyotyped and documented.

RESULTS
Karyotype: 46,XX

INTERPRETATION
Normal female chromosome complement. No evidence of trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) or other numerical or structural chromosomal abnormalities detected at this level of resolution.

This G-banded karyotype analysis confirms and supersedes the preliminary rapid PCR results. The normal female karyotype (46,XX) indicates no detectable chromosomal abnormalities that would be associated with common genetic syndromes including Down syndrome, Edwards syndrome, Patau syndrome, or sex chromosome aneuploidies.

LIMITATIONS
Conventional karyotyping can detect numerical abnormalities and structural rearrangements larger than approximately 5-10 Mb. Smaller deletions, duplications, or other subtle chromosomal changes may not be detected by this method. This test does not rule out single gene disorders, multifactorial conditions, or chromosomal mosaicism below the detection threshold.

Reported by: [redacted name], Ph.D., FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], M.D., Ph.D.
CAP Accredited Laboratory #[redacted ID]
